claims: The shared ordinary-turn and isolated-Lab selector now reports complete monotonic elapsed time, including lookup/filter and freshness assembly. The previous elapsedMs only reported the inner selection duration even though the existing deadline already included lookup. Separate lookup/filter and inner-selection measurements explain this discrepancy in protected Lab inspection through the unchanged bounded explanation schema.

The 10 ms deadline, contextual-detail expectation and all selection/privacy/correction criteria remain unchanged. Negative or nonfinite total/lookup elapsed time withholds optional content. Two new deterministic unit tests prove total accounting, exact deadline refusal, clock reversal and scope revocation; these tests do not certify latency.

Actual Lab runs still use the real performance clock. The source and browser suites ran concurrently with unchanged suite concurrency. Source assertions now preserve full failing synthetic rows; diagnostics retain complete real row measurements on successes and failures.

The newly instrumented run reproduced a deadline miss: ambiguous-pair/enabled took 29.345875 ms total, with 28.583708 ms lookup/filter and 0.691042 ms inner selection. It returned no optional detail and retained the failed expected-context check. The protected API case passed in the same suite and reported 1.929 ms total. This establishes a deadline failure in this run, not the precise SQL/CPU/scheduling cause or the cause of the older failure.
